title: A regular hyperplane section of a coherent module and its cohomology sequence
statement:
Let $k$ be an infinite field [def-weil-field], $n\geq1$, $P=\mathbf P^n_k$ with twists [def-pc-projective-space-twist], and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_P$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. There is a nonzero $s\in H^0(P,\mathcal O_P(1))$ whose zero scheme $i:H=Z(s)\hookrightarrow P$ [def-pc-zero-scheme] admits an isomorphism $H\cong\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$ carrying $i^*\mathcal O_P(d)$ to $\mathcal O_H(d)$ for every $d\in\mathbf Z$, compatibly with the multiplication maps $\mathcal O(d)\otimes\mathcal O(e)\to\mathcal O(d+e)$ on both sides. The module $\mathcal G=i^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is coherent and, for every integer $d$, multiplication by $s$ gives a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal F(d-1)\xrightarrow{\,s\,}\mathcal F(d)\longrightarrow i_*\mathcal G(d)\longrightarrow0.$$
With module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology], its long exact sequence is
$$0\longrightarrow H^0(P,\mathcal F(d-1))\xrightarrow{s}H^0(P,\mathcal F(d))\longrightarrow H^0(H,\mathcal G(d))\longrightarrow H^1(P,\mathcal F(d-1))\longrightarrow\cdots,$$
with consecutive terms
$$H^j(P,\mathcal F(d-1))\longrightarrow H^j(P,\mathcal F(d))\longrightarrow H^j(H,\mathcal G(d))\longrightarrow H^{j+1}(P,\mathcal F(d-1))$$
for all $j\geq0$. The maps to cohomology on $H$ are restriction maps. Restriction $H^0(P,\mathcal O_P(1))\longrightarrow H^0(H,\mathcal O_H(1))$ is surjective, and for global sections $u$ of $\mathcal F(d)$ and $v$ of $\mathcal O_P(1)$ one has $(uv)|_H=(u|_H)(v|_H)$.

proof.text: The structure module $\mathcal O_P$ is coherent. Indeed, the Proj definition identifies $U_j=D_+(T_j)$ with the spectrum of the degree-zero localization of $k[T_0,\ldots,T_n]$ at $T_j$. This ring is $k[x_l:l\ne j]$: send $x_l$ to $T_l/T_j$, and send a degree-zero monomial fraction $T^a/T_j^r$, $\sum a_l=r$, back to $\prod_{l\ne j}x_l^{a_l}$. These mutually inverse substitutions give the asserted polynomial ring. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and $k$; the finite-type algebra theorem therefore makes every chart ring Noetherian. The charts cover $P$ (a homogeneous prime avoiding the irrelevant ideal avoids at least one $T_j$), so $P$ is locally Noetherian. On each chart $\mathcal O_P$ is the module associated to its coordinate ring and is generated by $1$, hence is quasi-coherent of finite type. The coherent-versus-finite-type theorem now applies.

source.place: Tag 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian; polynomial chart computation as in varieties.tex Tag 08A0; algebra.tex Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence

proof.text: Apply the existing common-hyperplane theorem to the finite family $E_1=\mathcal F$, $E_2=\mathcal O_P$. Its hypotheses hold: the field is infinite, $n\ge1$, and both modules are coherent by the assumption and step 1. It gives a single nonzero $s=\sum a_jT_j$, the closed immersion $i:H=V(s)\hookrightarrow P$, an isomorphism $\varphi:\mathbf P^{n-1}_k\xrightarrow{\sim}H$ identifying the degree-one twists, and coherent $\mathcal G=i^*\mathcal F$. This $V(s)$ is precisely the required zero scheme: on $U_j$ the frame $T_j$ trivializes $\mathcal O_P(1)$ and $s$ has coefficient $s/T_j$; the defining dual map of the zero scheme therefore has image ideal $(s/T_j)$, which also defines $V(s)$ there. The local defining ideals agree on the cover, hence the closed subschemes agree.

source.place: Tags 08A0 and 089Z, lemma-exact-sequence-induction and lemma-hyperplane; remark-exact-sequence-induction for a finite family

proof.text: Choose the degree-one comparison $\theta_1:\varphi^*i^*\mathcal O_P(1)\cong\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{n-1}}(1)$ supplied in step 2. Choose all integer-degree comparisons coherently from this one. The twist-tensor node identifies degree $d$ twists with the $d$th tensor powers of degree one when $d\ge0$, and with powers of its dual when $d<0$; its frame formula also identifies the degree-zero twist with the structure module. Pullback commutes with these tensor products by the pullback-tensor node. More explicitly, locally choose a frame $a$ of $\varphi^*i^*\mathcal O_P(1)$ and a frame $b$ of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{n-1}}(1)$, and write $\theta_1(a)=c b$, where $c$ is a unit. In degree $d$ set $\theta_d(a^d)=c^d b^d$, interpreting negative powers by the dual frames. If the frames change by units, their degree-$d$ transition functions are the $d$th powers, so these formulas agree on overlaps and glue. Both routes around the multiplication comparison send $a^d\otimes a^e$ to $c^{d+e}b^{d+e}$, since $c^dc^e=c^{d+e}$ for all integers. Thus the isomorphism of $H$ with projective space identifies every twist compatibly with every multiplication map. This argument also applies when $n=1$, so the lower projective space has dimension zero.

source.place: Tag 01MT, lemma-apply-modules, and its local frame multiplication; modules.tex Tag 01CD, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; expands the all-twists comparison in varieties.tex Tag 0EGK

proof.text: For the first member $E_1=\mathcal F$, the common-hyperplane theorem gives, for every integer $d$, the short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F(d-1)\xrightarrow{s}\mathcal F(d)\to i_*(\mathcal G(d))\to0$. It also gives the natural identification $H^j(P,i_*\mathcal G(d))\cong H^j(H,\mathcal G(d))$ for every $j\ge0$ and says that the quotient arrows are restriction arrows. Apply the long exact cohomology sequence of the cohomology node to this short exact sequence and use these identifications. Its initial segment is $0\to H^0(P,\mathcal F(d-1))\xrightarrow{s}H^0(P,\mathcal F(d))\to H^0(H,\mathcal G(d))\to H^1(P,\mathcal F(d-1))$; in degree $j$ it has exactly the four consecutive terms displayed in the item. Use the compatible comparisons of step 3 when viewing $\mathcal G(d)$ on $\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$.

source.place: Tag 0EGK, remark-exact-sequence-induction-cohomology, using the natural cohomology identification already in the common-hyperplane node

proof.text: Use the same theorem for the second member $E_2=\mathcal O_P$ and $d=1$. Its cohomology sequence includes $H^0(P,\mathcal O_P(1))\to H^0(H,\mathcal O_H(1))\to H^1(P,\mathcal O_P)$. Here $i^*\mathcal O_P=\mathcal O_H$: on any local ring map $A\to B$, the map $B\otimes_A A\to B$ sends $b\otimes a$ to $ba$, with inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. The projective-twist cohomology node, clause (iii) at twist zero, gives $H^1(P,\mathcal O_P)=0$. Exactness now proves the required surjectivity of the restriction of linear sections. This works for $n=1$ as well as for larger $n$.

source.place: Tags 01XS and 01XT, lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, with varieties.tex Tag 0EGK at E=O and d=1

proof.text: Finally the restriction maps just used are induced by the pullback unit. In a local trivialization their action is $u\mapsto1\otimes u$. The section formula in the pullback-tensor node sends $1\otimes(u\otimes v)$ to $(1\otimes u)\otimes(1\otimes v)$. Applying the twist multiplication map proves $(uv)|_H=(u|_H)(v|_H)$ as sections of $\mathcal G(d+1)$. The degree comparisons from step 3 preserve multiplication, so this equality also holds after identifying $H$ with $\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$. Thus all restriction and multiplication clauses use the same chosen hyperplane and twist comparisons.

source.place: Tag 01CD, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, section formula; constructions.tex Tag 01MT, multiplication of twists

tool_uses.why: Generic coherent iff quasi-coherent finite-type criterion on a locally Noetherian scheme, used only to make O_P a second member of the finite family; the unit has no replacement for this local module criterion.
Canonical frame multiplication of integer projective twists, used to make the degree-one comparison compatible in all degrees; a projective-geometry tool below the fixed Hilbert/regularity route.
Generic monoidal pullback and its actual section formula, used for tensor powers and multiplicative restriction; does not replace a step of the unit route.
Only H^1(P,O_P)=0 is used to turn the common-hyperplane cohomology sequence into surjectivity on degree-one sections; the unit contains no independent twist-cohomology calculation.
